note: Per-slide narration for the self-paced and SCORM editions. Instructional voice: each track sets up the page, explains the content, tells the learner what to do, and hands them a breadcrumb to the next page. Edit the text, push to main, and the generate-narration workflow re-creates assets/audio/narr-<id>.mp3 for each section and rebuilds the SCORM package. voice_id is an ElevenLabs voice; swap it to change the narrator.

sections.s-hero: Welcome to the Talent Marketplace course. This is a short, self-paced experience: about fifteen minutes, eight pages, and you are in control. Move between pages with the arrows at the bottom right, or by scrolling. On each page, press the Listen button and I will walk you through it. Here is where we are headed: first the why, then what the marketplace is, the six ways in, the process, the culture promises, and finally your personal plan. When you are ready, move to the next page and we will start with why this matters to Vanderbilt.
sections.s-charge: This page is the foundation for everything that follows. Read the headline first: Vanderbilt will define the great university of the twenty-first century, and be it. Below it are the three areas of focus that make that real: exceptional core operations, bold strategic initiatives, and values leadership. Notice the thread that runs through all three: talent. Every one of these depends on people who keep growing, and that is exactly what the marketplace is for. Take a moment with each card, then continue to the next page, where we answer the big question: what is the Talent Marketplace?
sections.s-what: Here is the heart of the course. The Talent Marketplace is Vanderbilt's home for growing your career inside the university, and this page shows you it is two things in one. Look at the first card: careers of interest. That is the long game: name where you want to grow, build toward it, and see openings before the public does. Now the second card: short projects in other units that build your skills while your home job stays yours. That is the short game. Below them, read the promises: everything stays private until you act, and leaders only ever see group totals. Before you leave this page, scroll down and play the fact or fiction game. It takes one minute and it will show you what most people get wrong. When you finish, move on to find your own way in.
sections.s-entrances: Now make it personal. This page shows six doors into the marketplace, and they group into three kinds of talent. Looking to grow covers the curious, the plateaued, and the ready. Hidden talent is for people who are great in their role but have skills the role never asks for. Not a fit but right mission is for people after a reorg, or whose role is at risk. Here is what to do: tap each door to open it and read the path inside, first conversation to landed move. Then pick the door closest to your situation today; yours might be a mix. Notice that every door starts the same way: a growth conversation with your manager. Try the matching game at the bottom to test yourself, then continue to the next page to see the full process.
sections.s-process: This page shows the rhythm of the marketplace, and it is simpler than most people expect. There are two beats. The first beat is every day: keep your skills honest and current, flag your careers of interest, and take learning tied to your goals. The second beat is when opportunity arises: staff see eligible openings first, the interviews are fair, and a chosen move ends with a planned handoff. Read both columns, then play the call the next move game below to walk through real moments in order. The lesson to carry: growth is daily, and readiness is the reward. When you are done, move to the next page for the part managers care about most: the culture.
sections.s-culture: This page matters most if you lead people, but it protects everyone, so stay with me. Start with the research at the top: about three out of four managers admit to holding on to strong team members, and that pressure stops people from moving inside. That is why the promises on this page are plain. No retaliation, ever. No watching. And managers coach: the model response is thank you for telling me, what drew you to it, and how can I help you prepare well? Read the three stat cards to see why releasing talent is a leadership win, then play the response game: you will hear five manager lines and decide which build the culture and which break it. When you can hear the difference, you are ready for the last step: your plan.
sections.s-plan: This is your page. Everything so far becomes action here, in two steps. Step one: take the recap quiz at the top. Six questions, instant feedback, and your score is recorded, so give it real attention. Step two: work the five moves below the quiz. Have a growth conversation with your manager. Build a plan with the Talent Marketplace tool. Update your career preferences in Oracle. Make sure your skills are current and honestly leveled. And flag your careers of interest in the Grow area. Each card links to the real screen in Oracle, and the screenshots show you exactly what you will see. Before you leave, select print the job aid so the five moves go with you. Then move to the final page to close out.
sections.s-close: You made it. Let us put the whole course in one breath. The Talent Marketplace is Vanderbilt's home for your growth and development: identify where you want to grow, build the skills with your manager's support, and pursue opportunities inside the university when they arise. Your activity stays private until you act, and the promises protect you the whole way. Your one next step is already on your list: a conversation with your manager about your growth and development. Schedule it this week. This course is complete, and your progress has been recorded. Thank you for spending fifteen minutes on your future here. Now go grow.
